response.sql: WITH gender_counts AS (SELECT c.gender, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM Orders o JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.date_order_placed BETWEEN '2013-10-25 17:40:25' AND '2017-05-24 19:26:44' GROUP BY c.gender), avg_count AS (SELECT AVG(order_count) AS avg_order_count FROM gender_counts) SELECT g.gender, g.order_count, g.order_count - a.avg_order_count AS above_average_by FROM gender_counts g CROSS JOIN avg_count a WHERE g.order_count > a.avg_order_count;

assumptions.assumption: date_order_placed is stored as text in 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' form, so the BETWEEN comparison is a text comparison and its bounds are inclusive, as the request specifies.

The average is the mean of the per-gender order counts across the genders that have at least one qualifying order. A NULL customer gender forms its own group. The request does not say how to treat NULL gender.
The inner join to Customers enforces 'customers that exist', so orders with no matching customer are excluded.
